To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a mitotic inhibitor, MW 30 000–50 000 is present in the culture medium of mouse embryo cells and is increased in amount with increase in P.D.L. and that it inhibits DNA synthesis in cells at all P.D.L. tested, but is effective only against low-P.D.L. target cells.
the activity of the fibroblast mitosis inhibitor extracted from mouse embryo fibroblasts increases with increase in PdLs and becomes potent against cultures at any PdL.
the activity of a mitotic inhibitor extracted from subconfluent mouse embryo fibroblasts increases with the population doubling level of the culture and is effective against all PDL target cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a study of changes in activity of mitotic inhibitor in fibroblasts of mouse embryo cultures aging in vitro and transformed spontaneously in vivo.
the role of the mitotic inhibitor in the regulation of the cell division cycle in mouse embryonic cells in vitro.
the role of mitotic inhibitors in cell aging and transformation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the inhibitor activity extracted from cultures of different PDL is not a single entity.

the inhibitor activity extracted from the highest PDL culture was most effective in suppressing mitosis of all cultures tested, whereas the inhibitor from the lowest Pdl culture was effective only in inhibiting mitosis in the lowest PDL cultures.

the mitotic inhibitor activity of the extract from a given number cells increases with increase in PRL of the donor culture and becomes active against cultures of all PDLs, whereas the extract from the lowest-PDL culture is effective against cultures only at lower PDLs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

in the mouse embryo fibroblasts aging in vitro and spontaneously transformed, the accumulation of a tissue-specific mitotic inhibitor is an event of the in vitro aging and is not associated with the in vitro transformation.

the accumulation of the inhibitor may be a cause of the decreased mitotic activity in the aging cells, but the decrease of the inhibitor activity in the spontaneously transformed culture may be the cause of its increased growth rate.
in vitro aging and in vivo malignancy are not necessarily linked and that the mitotic inhibitor may be a marker for in vitro aging and a potential tool for the study of its mechanism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a significant increase in the amount of mitotic inhibitor produced by the cells as they age in vitro.
the inhibitor is a potent inhibitor of mitosis in all PDLs, and that its accumulation in aging cultures may contribute to the decrease in cell growth rate and eventual death.
the mitotic inhibitor is a potent inhibitor of the proliferation of cancer cells, and it is possible that the accumulation of the inhibitor in the aging process may contribute to cancer resistance.
